changed: PATCH 0.41.3 adds a separate native-video diagnostic page at /player-diagnostic.html, without changing the homepage, media delivery route or approved media bytes. Player A uses a literal video src attribute; Player B uses a literal child source element. Neither uses an app framework, poster, caption track or custom playback handler.

The page observes native playback states with named constants so NETWORK_NO_SOURCE is not mistaken for a count of errors. A user-triggered, credential-free same-origin request for bytes 0–1 displays HTTP status, media type, range, length and received byte count. It times out after ten seconds and cancels an unexpectedly large response after a small bounded read. This fetch is a separate diagnostic, not evidence that the browser media stack succeeded.

The preceding 0.41.2 DEV release at main 1c50e010bf4eb6057a1c59090a25dc0a3e47d3e0 passed source review and Chrome playback, but the real iPhone Safari embed still reported source failure, no metadata and NETWORK_NO_SOURCE. The same iPhone played both the original CDN URL and the new same-origin URL directly. These observations narrow the problem but do not identify its cause or clear the embedded first-byte request path.

Local diagnostic fixtures passed four tests: literal native player patterns and no custom initialization; named failure-state observation; user-triggered fixed two-byte request with no credentials; bounded cancellation when the server returns too much data. Existing source-suite evidence belongs to 0.41.2 and is not relabeled as the final diagnostic release checks.

Fixed diagnostic scenario denominator 3: iPhone visitor plays A; iPhone visitor plays B; visitor runs the separate first-byte response check. Candidate DEV-browser and physical-iPhone layers each attempted 0, passed 0, failed 0, untested 3. Production is not targeted. This is DEV-only diagnostic publication, not a claimed playback fix. User native testing must inform the next change; production stays unchanged. All 132 older release entries and accepted notes remain intact. No unrelated frozen work is included.
security: The diagnostic sends no telemetry or report, collects no user data, reads no app credentials or storage, and never changes playback programmatically. Its sole explicit fetch has a hard-coded same-origin public media path and credentials omitted. Response text is rendered with textContent; response bodies are not displayed. No authentication, schema, permissions, bindings, security settings, deployment trigger or external media target changes.
